title: Preemptive scale-order smoothing to prevent small-tenant reservation squeeze
creator: Amrita Shah
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent coldstarts and degraded throughput during a multi-region surge. Root cause: preemption ordering in the scale-down path allowed recently-warmed small-tenant reservations to be preempted ahead of older low-utilization allocations, which combined with an early-scale-down window in the autoscaler and a conservative burst reclamation policy produced silent capacity loss for low-cardinality tenants. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations, and permanent fixes deployed to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-12 03:12 UTC - Alert: Ops received multiple customer escalations (large SaaS customer and two mid-market tenants) reporting elevated 503s and request latencies on dedicated clusters in us-west-2.
2026-02-12 03:25 UTC - Pager duty acknowledged; on-call infra lead (Liam) started triage. Initial hypothesis: reserved pool exhaustion due to surge.

2026-02-12 04:00 UTC - Confirmed spike in allocation churn and increase in preemption events correlating with autoscaler scale-down waves. Telemetry showed small-tenant reservations (<=8 slots) were losing slots disproportionately.

2026-02-12 05:10 UTC - Mitigation: disabled aggressive early-scale-down heuristic and relaxed per-tenant preemption scores to prefer older allocations. Short-term config rolled out to us-west-2 and us-east-1.
2026-02-12 06:30 UTC - Customer comms: first status update sent to affected customers; we indicated investigation and temporary mitigations.

2026-02-13 - Engineering deep-dive: captured allocator traces, preemption decision logs, and autoscaler event windows. Identified two contributing issues: (1) preemption comparator used a timestamp that was updated on warmup completion (so freshly-warmed reservations appeared newer and therefore more preemptable), and (2) autoscaler early-scale-down algorithm did not account for recent warmup credit deductions and followed a conservative burst reclaim schedule.

2026-02-15 - Patch proposed: (A) change preemption comparator to prefer allocations with lower effective remaining-burst-credit and older "creation" timestamp (separate from warmup-complete timestamp); (B) introduce a 3m grace window after warmup before allocations become eligible for preemption; (C) autoscaler update to include a warmup-aware headroom projection to avoid early scale-down during high churn.

2026-02-18 - Code review: PRs #r/gh 4823 and 4824 opened. Design and PM reviewed trade-offs: grace window avoids immediate preemption at cost of slightly higher transient headroom usage; approved for rollout after canary.
2026-02-20 - Canary rollout to a single shard in us-west-2. Observed decreased preemption of small tenants and normalized request success rates for canary shard.

2026-02-22 - Gradual rollout to all dedicated clusters over 6 hours with monitoring gates. No regressions observed. Follow-up: add fallback metrics to detect over-provisioning (headroom burn) and tune grace window if needed.
2026-03-01 - Postmortem drafted, customers given detailed RCA and timeline. Credits issued to affected customers per escalation policy.
2026-03-10 - Ticket closed after follow-ups: new integration tests, runbook updates, and a scheduled 6-week bake period for the autoscaler change.

acceptance_criteria: Root cause fixed: Preemption comparator and autoscaler headroom projection updated and merged
Automated tests covering comparator logic and warmup grace window added to CI
Canary + full rollout completed with no customer regressions
Runbook updated with steps to detect and mitigate small-tenant reservation squeeze
Customer communications sent and credits processed for affected accounts
postmortem_summary: Cause: two interacting bugs in the scale-down path causing systematic preemption of freshly-warmed small-tenant allocations. Fix: separate allocation creation timestamp from warmup completion, add a 3-minute warmup grace window, and update autoscaler headroom projection. Outcome: decreased customer-facing coldstarts, no measurable long-term cost hit in 6-week bake. Follow-ups: allocation-level auditing, more robust churn simulations in CI, longer-term autoscaler model improvements (ENG-710001).
